# Omit

Builds, for each object in an array, a new object without the listed fields.

## Signature

```jyro
# fragment
Omit(items, fields)
```

| Parameter | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | array | The array to read. Null is read as an empty array. Elements that are not objects are left out. Any other type that is not an array is a runtime error. |
| `fields` | array | An array of the field names to remove, each matched exactly against the keys, case included. Elements that are not strings are ignored. Null is read as an empty array, which removes nothing. |

## Returns

Array. A new array with one new object for each object in items, in order, holding every other field of that object in its original order. Never null.

## Example

`Omit([{ "a": 1, "b": 2 }], ["b"])` returns `[{ "a": 1 }]`.
